messages:
alex: FYI customer MegaForm hitting a big tail-latency spike after we rolled GreenNova yesterday. They see p95~600ms -> 2s and p99 up to ~8s on long requests (~12k+ tokens). Ticket #5467 created.

alex: @tess can you pull the per-route breakdown? They call /v1/generate with streaming off.

ops-bot: Deploy green-nova v2 (gn-bpe-v2 tokenizer) to prod completed by deploy-bot at 2026-03-15T09:38:21Z :rocket:

tess: Looking at dashboard — the jump aligns with the deploy window. The spike is concentrated on the generate runner nodes (gpu-pool-b). Latency curve shows a clear inflection when input token count > ~11k. CPU on tokenizers is spiking.

tess: Quick snippet from trace histogram: ```
route: /v1/generate
model: green-nova-v2
p50: 120ms
p95: 2.1s
p99: 7.8s
avg input tokens: 13.2k
tokenizer_cpu: 82% (on tokenizer-worker)
kv-cache-hits: down 18% vs baseline
```

jasper: We swapped the tokenization pipeline to gn-bpe-v2 to fix some multibyte edge cases. That variant is more aggressive in subtoken expansion for rare unicode sequences — could blow up token counts for long docs. If token count balloons, KV cache gets invalidated more often and runtime falls back to slow path.

liam: I repro'd a similar spike locally. Minimal repro: send a ~14k-token markdown doc that contains lots of rare unicode emojis and CJK lines. With gn-bpe-v2 the token count jumps ~1.6x vs gn-bpe-v1 and generation latency p99 increases accordingly. Repro command:```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"green-nova-v2","input":"<long-doc-with-emoji-and-cjk>","max_tokens":512}'
```

liam: Attached local run logs show KV cache misses and a fallback to the long-sequence slow decoder: ```
[2026-03-15T09:45:10Z] tokenizer: input_tokens=14023 -> subtokens=22468
[2026-03-15T09:45:10Z] runtime: kv_cache_hit=false, falling back to full attention slowpath
[2026-03-15T09:45:11Z] decoder: step 1 latency=120ms
[2026-03-15T09:45:18Z] decoder: step 25 latency=7.3s (p99)
```

alex: Thanks — sounds like tokenizer variant is the smoking gun. Two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) rollout a hotfix that pins the tokenizer to gn-bpe-v1 for GreenNova while we investigate; 2) enable model fallback to green-nova-lite for requests with >10k tokens. Thoughts?

jasper: Agree. We can push a config hotfix in the control plane to set tokenizer: gn-bpe-v1 for green-nova model family. That is low-risk and reversible. Also add a temporary routing rule: if input_tokens_est > 10k, route to green-nova-lite (smaller context-optimized variant).

tess: Ops note — pinning tokenizer requires a small deploy to tokenizer workers (rolling restart of tokenizer workers in region-us-east-1). Will take ~6m with standard draining. I can schedule now.

liam: I'll prepare an automated repro script that sanitizes customer payloads (removes PII) and demonstrates token inflation between v1/v2. That will help quantify regressions and validate the rollback.

alex: I'll inform MegaForm that we're investigating and plan a short config rollback. ETA 20–30m.

ops-bot: Action queued: rollback tokenizer variant for model green-nova to gn-bpe-v1 (control-plane change). Request by alex. Change ID: CP-9876.

jasper: I'll also add a metric to alert on tokenizer-subtoken-ratio > 1.3 for a model — should catch regressions earlier.

tess: Rolling now. Draining node 4/8, 5/8...

liam: Ran quick check after controlling tokenizer to v1 in staging: token counts normalize, p99 drops from ~7s -> ~650ms on the same sample.

alex: Customer notified: "we're rolling a minor config change to revert tokenizer behavior and will follow up with a full postmortem." They replied :thumbsup:.

jasper: Next steps: (1) rollback in prod (inflight) (2) reproduce with sanitized customer data and submit quant results (liam) (3) add tokenizer-ratio alert (jasper) (4) prepare a canary test in the CI that exercises rare-unicode-heavy docs (tess)

alex: Assigning owners: jasper (hotfix + alert), tess (rollout ops), liam (repro + report), alex (customer comms). Will update ticket #5467.

tess: Rollout complete. All tokenizer workers back to steady state. Preliminary dashboard shows p95/p99 returning to baseline.

liam: Confirmed on staging-sized sample and a quick check on a subset of customer traffic: p99 reduced to ~700ms.

alex: Great work team. We'll keep the ticket open for the postmortem and follow-on mitigations (canary, CI tests, alert thresholds).
